title: Special Act on the Restoration of Honor of Participants in the Donghak Peasant Revolution and Others
title_original: 동학농민혁명 참여자 등의 명예회복에 관한 특별법
full_text:
Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Act is to inspire the national spirit by honoring, inheriting and developing the patriotic spirit and devotion to the Korean people of those who participated in the Donghak Peasant Revolution to reform the feudal system and defend national sovereignty against Japanese imperialist aggression, and to restore the honor of participants in the Donghak Peasant Revolution and their surviving family members.

Article 2 (Definitions)
The terms used in this Act shall be defined as follows:
1. "Participants in the Donghak Peasant Revolution" means participants in the peasant-led revolution that launched its first uprising in March 1894 to reform the feudal system and its second uprising in September of the same year to wage an armed struggle against Japan in defense of national sovereignty against Japanese imperialist aggression.
2. "Surviving family members" means the children, grandchildren, great-grandchildren and great-great-grandchildren of participants in the Donghak Peasant Revolution.

Article 3 (Committee for Deliberation on Restoration of Honor of Participants in the Donghak Peasant Revolution)
(1) A Committee for Deliberation on Restoration of Honor of Participants in the Donghak Peasant Revolution (hereinafter referred to as the "Committee") shall be established under the Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism to deliberate and decide on determination and registration of participants in the Donghak Peasant Revolution and their surviving family members. <Amended December 19, 2017>
(2) Deleted. <December 19, 2017>
(3) The Committee shall consist of no more than nine members, including one chairperson. The Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism shall appoint or commission members from among relevant public officials, representatives of surviving family members, and persons with extensive knowledge and experience, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, and shall appoint the chairperson from among the members. <Amended December 19, 2017>
(4) The term of office of a member who is not a public official shall be three years, and the member may be reappointed or recommissioned. <Added December 19, 2017>
(5) The term of office of a replacement member who is not a public official shall be the remainder of the predecessor's term. <Added December 19, 2017>
(6) Matters necessary for operation of the Committee shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended December 19, 2017>

Article 4 (Dismissal and Decommissioning of Members)
The Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism may dismiss or decommission a member of the Committee in any of the following cases:
1. Where the member becomes unable to perform duties due to a mental or physical disability.
2. Where misconduct relating to the member's duties is found.
3. Where the member is considered unsuitable to remain in office due to neglect of duties, loss of dignity or other reasons.
4. Where the member expresses that it is difficult to perform the duties.

Article 5 (Registration of Surviving Family Members)
(1) A person seeking recognition as a surviving family member shall apply to the Committee for registration as a surviving family member, attaching the relevant documents prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended December 19, 2017>
(2) Upon receiving an application for registration under paragraph (1), the Committee shall deliberate and decide on it by the end of December of the year following the year in which the application was received. <Amended December 19, 2017>
(3) Deleted. <December 19, 2017>

Article 6 (Fact-Finding)
Where necessary to deliberate and decide on matters under its jurisdiction, the Committee may hear statements from applicants for registration as surviving family members or persons with relevant information, or conduct verification or fact-finding investigations. <Amended December 19, 2017>

Article 7 (Duty of Relevant Institutions to Cooperate)
To collect materials relating to the Donghak Peasant Revolution, the Committee may request relevant institutions to permit inspection of or provide materials and similar assistance, and the institutions shall comply unless there is a special reason. <Amended December 19, 2017>

Article 8 (Commemorative Projects)
The Government shall promote the following projects to carry on the patriotic spirit and devotion to the Korean people of participants in the Donghak Peasant Revolution: <Amended December 19, 2017>
1. Construction of a Donghak Peasant Revolution memorial hall, memorial monument, memorial park and other commemorative facilities.
2. Academic research and exchanges relating to the Donghak Peasant Revolution.
3. Improvement of historic sites of the Donghak Peasant Revolution.
4. Projects to restore the honor of participants in the Donghak Peasant Revolution and their surviving family members.

Article 9 (Donghak Peasant Revolution Memorial Foundation)
(1) The Donghak Peasant Revolution Memorial Foundation (hereinafter referred to as the "Memorial Foundation") shall be established with approval from the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism to promote commemorative projects relating to the Donghak Peasant Revolution.
(2) The Memorial Foundation shall be a legal entity.
(3) The Memorial Foundation shall have officers and necessary staff as prescribed by its articles of incorporation.
(4) The Memorial Foundation shall conduct the following projects:
1. Operation of a Donghak Peasant Revolution memorial hall and archive.
2. Commemorative and memorial projects for the Donghak Peasant Revolution.
3. Collection, management, preservation, exhibition and exchange of materials relating to the Donghak Peasant Revolution.
4. Projects to restore the honor of participants in the Donghak Peasant Revolution and their surviving family members.
5. Improvement of historic sites of the Donghak Peasant Revolution.
6. Establishment and operation of a Donghak Peasant Revolution research institute.
7. Other projects consistent with the purpose of carrying on the spirit of the Donghak Peasant Revolution.
(5) Where necessary to develop a Donghak Peasant Revolution memorial park, the State or a local government may grant State or public property (limited to land) to the Memorial Foundation free of charge, notwithstanding the State Property Act and the Public Property and Commodity Management Act. In such cases, the existing designated use of the State or public property so granted shall be deemed discontinued without a separate procedure for discontinuance of use. <Amended December 19, 2017>
(6) Where State or public property is granted free of charge under paragraph (5), the details, conditions, procedures and other matters shall be determined by a contract between the management authority of the property and the Memorial Foundation. <Added December 19, 2017>
(7) The State and local governments may, within budgetary limits, support expenses necessary for performance of the Memorial Foundation's projects and duties. <Added December 19, 2017>
(8) Except as provided in this Act, the provisions of the Civil Act concerning incorporated foundations shall apply mutatis mutandis to the Memorial Foundation. <Amended December 19, 2017>

Article 10 (Entrustment of Committee Operation and Administrative Affairs)
(1) The Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism may entrust operation of the Committee and handling of its administrative affairs to the Memorial Foundation as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(2) When entrusting operation of the Committee and handling of its administrative affairs under paragraph (1), the Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism may support the necessary expenses.

Article 11 (Deemed Public Officials for Application of Penalty Provisions)
Members of the Committee who are not public officials, and officers and staff of the Memorial Foundation engaged in duties entrusted by the Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism under Article 10, shall be deemed public officials when Articles 127 and 129 through 132 of the Criminal Act apply.

Addenda <Act No. 7177, March 5, 2004>
This Act shall enter into force on the date six months after its promulgation.

Addenda <Act No. 8277, January 26, 2007>
Article 1 (Enforcement Date) This Act shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation. However, the amended provisions of Article 9 shall enter into force on January 1, 2010.
Article 2 (Special Cases for Applications for Registration of Surviving Family Members) Notwithstanding Article 5(1), a person seeking recognition as a surviving family member may apply to the Working Committee for registration as a surviving family member within six months from the enforcement date of this Act.
Article 3 (Transitional Measures for the Donghak Peasant Revolution Memorial Foundation)
(1) The incorporated Donghak Peasant Revolution Memorial Foundation established with approval from the Minister of Culture and Tourism under Article 32 of the Civil Act as of the enforcement of this Act shall prepare articles of incorporation for the Memorial Foundation under this Act and obtain approval from the Minister of Culture and Tourism within two months after January 1, 2010.
(2) Upon obtaining approval under paragraph (1), the incorporated Donghak Peasant Revolution Memorial Foundation shall register establishment of the Memorial Foundation under this Act.
(3) Upon completing registration of establishment under paragraph (2), the incorporated Donghak Peasant Revolution Memorial Foundation shall be deemed dissolved notwithstanding the provisions of the Civil Act concerning dissolution and liquidation of legal entities.
(4) The Memorial Foundation under this Act shall succeed to all rights, obligations and property of the incorporated Donghak Peasant Revolution Memorial Foundation on the date of registration of establishment.
(5) The officers and staff of the incorporated Donghak Peasant Revolution Memorial Foundation as of the enforcement of this Act shall be deemed officers and staff of the Memorial Foundation under this Act, and their terms shall be calculated from their respective previous appointment dates.

Addenda (Government Organization Act) <Act No. 8852, February 29, 2008>
Article 1 (Enforcement Date) This Act shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation. However, ... <omitted> ..., among the Acts amended under Article 6 of the Addenda, provisions amending an Act promulgated before this Act enters into force but not yet in force shall enter into force on the enforcement date of that respective Act.
Articles 2 through 5 omitted.
Article 6 (Amendment of Other Acts) Paragraphs (1) through (253) omitted.
(254) The Special Act on the Restoration of Honor of Participants in the Donghak Peasant Revolution and Others shall be partially amended as follows:
In Article 9(1), "Minister of Culture and Tourism" shall be replaced with "Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism."
Paragraphs (255) through (760) omitted.
Article 7 omitted.

Addenda <Act No. 10110, March 17, 2010>
This Act shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.

Addenda <Act No. 15262, December 19, 2017>
Article 1 (Enforcement Date) This Act shall enter into force on the date three months after its promulgation.
Article 2 (Special Cases Concerning Committee Members) Notwithstanding Article 3(1) of the Addenda, the terms of Committee members appointed or commissioned under the previous Article 3(3) before this Act enters into force shall be deemed to expire on the day before the enforcement date of this Act.
Article 3 (Transitional Measures Concerning the Committee and Related Bodies)
(1) The Committee under the previous provisions as of the enforcement of this Act shall be deemed the Committee under the amended Article 3(1).
(2) Acts of the Committee and the Working Committee under the previous provisions before this Act enters into force shall be deemed acts of the Committee under the amended Article 3(1).
